change.behavior: Session.transfer_claim correlates the durable lease.transferred event with the Store transfer request identity and avoids appending the same transition again when a caller retries after the claim batch and event are durable but the sender snapshot save failed.
change.provenance: The event includes the stable transfer_request_id already admitted and recorded by the atomic claims transfer operation.
change.authority: No claim authority or filesystem permission was broadened. Test fixtures that request claim acquisition now declare writable intent; a no-authority entry test continues to assert denial.

checks: python3 -m py_compile mncs_env/sessions.py tests/test_store_claim_transfer.py tests/test_entry.py tests/test_doctor.py: passed
ruff check --select F401,F821,F822,F823 mncs_env/sessions.py tests/test_store_claim_transfer.py tests/test_entry.py tests/test_doctor.py: passed

interruption_case.store: isolated test-owned Store under pytest temporary directory
interruption_case.interruption_point: after atomic claim transfer and transfer-event persistence, before sender snapshot publication

canonical_environment.canonical_store_transport: authenticated Environment RPC through MNCS Control

limits: The new session-level retry regression uses an isolated test-owned Store and does not itself constitute a canonical Store transfer test.
Existing crash-boundary and competing-recipient tests cover the atomic claims transfer protocol; this new test covers retry after the durable transfer when snapshot publication fails.
Canonical Store service-process termination and restart during publication remain unproven.
The duplicate Environment session for this campaign remains retained and untouched; this evidence applies to the selected authenticated session.
